At about 4:30 p.m. Feb. 18th. 1938, Mr. Wong Bang (汪鵬) called at Police Headquarters, where he stated that he had received information, contained in an anonymous letter, to the effect that certain persons named, Soo Kan Zien (蘇簡先), Zee Ping Fong (徐品芳), Zee Chia Pau (齊家寶) and Zee Chia Foo (齊家富) were planning to kidnap him. It later transpired that this letter had actually been written by one named Hsu Zau Tseong (許兆昌), who was known to the complainant, but in order to protect this man, Mr. Wong had agreed not to divulge his name.

It appears that Mr. Wong prior to becoming compradores of the Bus Company, was formerly adjutant to General Yang Hu, Shanghai and Woosung Garrison Commander. Following the retreat of the Chinese Forces from the Shanghai Area, former subordinates of the Garrison Commander's Headquarters and S.C.G.P. Bureau, working in conjunction with Japanese or Koreans, had kidnapped and held to ransom former high officials of the above organisations. Large sums of money had apparently been extorted from these officials by threats of handing them over to the Japanese Military Authorities on trumped up charges of having conspired against them. Korean and the 2nd. accused, on being arraigned before their respective Courts will undoubtedly plead that they know nothing of this plot and that they met together in the Central Hotel in order to discuss a proposed sugar deal. This, as the 4th. accused can testify, is correct, but the primary cause of the visit was to discuss the plans for the kidnapping of Mr. Wong Bang.

The 1st. accused refuses to make a statement and seeks to throw the blame for this conspiracy onto his nephew, the 4th.accused. That, the 1st. accused, a well known loafer and former detective of the S.C.G.P.Bureau, could be coerced by a mere youth into taking part in a plot of this nature is ridiculous, and a plea of this kind should be totally disregarded.

In spite of the efforts made by detectives attached to this branch, no trace of Hau Tsu Tsong (高祖宗), the person who first wrote to the complainant, informing him of this plot, has been found. This man was formerly a clerk employed by the late Shanghai and Woosung Garrison Commander's Headquarters, and therefore, was well acquainted with the complainant. It is imperative that this man be located as he apparently can give information relating to previous kidnappings alleged to have been carried out by the persons now in custody.

The 5th. accused, Zee Chia Fah (方家發), was identified as an employee of the Bus Co. who on the 15th. Feb. 1938, sent a letter to him requesting an appointment. On the 18th. Feb. 1938, at about 5 p.m. he met the 5th. accused outside the Jessfield Park, who confided in him the plot to kidnap his brother. He also informed Mr. Wong that the gang, who were plotting to kidnap his brother, were led by Zee Hai Dee and that they were previously concerned in the kidnapping of two former officers of the local Garrison Commander's Staff, named Chou (邱) and Wong (王).
